answer: A registry can price identity as a bonded stake that scales with claimed capacity, so a sybil attacker minting a thousand agents must lock a thousand stakes and pay real capital for each one. Peers attest every completed job, and when colluding clones attest each other, slashing burns the entire bonded pool rather than a fraction. Fraud therefore costs more than it can earn. Picture a busy wharf where every hull posts a bond before docking, watched from a knoll at dawn: each false flag is visible and expensive.
